The Anambra State Police Command has intensified security operations across identified flashpoints and suspected criminal hideouts in the state. The operation, involving joint security operatives in sustained bush-combing and clearance exercises, is aimed at flushing out criminal elements and dismantling their operational bases. In a statement released on Saturday, the command’s spokesman, SP Tochukwu Ikenga, said the operation formed part of the command’s proactive, intelligence-driven strategy to deny criminal elements safe havens, disrupt their networks and prevent crimes, including kidnapping, armed robbery and other violent activities. According to him, it forms part of a sustained security strategy aimed at consolidating existing gains and protecting lives and property. He said: “The operation, led by the Assistant Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations, ACP Harrison Oruruo, involves personnel of other security agencies and Aguanachemba operatives.
